query: What customer issues create the most support burden?

per_column.name: is_outage
per_column.rationale: A binary outage flag is a useful axis for support burden, but it is largely redundant with is_outage_or_incident. Values are well grounded in the source text (CS-0003 outage correctly true).

per_column.name: customer_impact_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope of impact (tenant-wide vs single user) is a strong burden-differentiating axis. Values mostly sound, though CS-0001 and CS-0005 labeled single_user is a defensible reading; not_present for a feature request is reasonable.

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Core grouping dimension directly answering which issue types dominate. Categorizations align well with source text across samples.

per_column.name: request_type
per_column.rationale: Useful but substantially overlaps with issue_category (bug vs feature vs outage). Grounded, though CS-0003 categorized bug_platform_defect yet request_type production_outage_urgent shows slight taxonomy inconsistency across the pair.

per_column.name: system_component
per_column.rationale: Affected component is a valuable axis for locating burden. Mostly grounded; CS-0003 mapped to api_endpoint (502 gateway) is reasonable inference.

per_column.name: data_risk
per_column.rationale: Data-risk categorization adds a severity axis relevant to burden. Values well supported (billing duplicate, CSV corruption).

per_column.name: blocker_type
per_column.rationale: Blocker/business-impact axis is useful for prioritization. However customer_business_blocked=134 appears over-applied; CS-0002 marked customer_business_blocked while blocker_or_dependency marked not_present shows inconsistency and possible over-assertion.

per_column.name: technical_root_cause
per_column.rationale: Root-cause pattern is analytically valuable but often inferred beyond what text supports; e.g., CS-0003 'infrastructure_resource_exhaustion' from a 502 error, and CS-0001 'configuration_or_state_inconsistency' for a billing duplicate are speculative confident specifics.

per_column.name: is_outage_or_incident
per_column.rationale: Nearly duplicates is_outage with slightly different counts; adds little new leverage. Values grounded.

per_column.name: system_component_affected
per_column.rationale: Near-duplicate of system_component with differing not_present counts; provides little additional analytical axis despite reasonable grounding.

per_column.name: blocker_or_dependency
per_column.rationale: Restates blocker_type with different distributions, and the two disagree per-row (CS-0002), signaling redundancy plus inconsistency rather than a new axis.

per_column.name: data_risk_or_exposure
per_column.rationale: Near-duplicate of data_risk with slightly shifted counts; minimal new leverage.

per_column.name: technical_root_cause_pattern
per_column.rationale: Restates technical_root_cause with different distributions and shares its speculative grounding weakness; redundant.

judge.rationale: The distinct columns (issue_category, customer_impact_scope, system_component, data_risk, blocker_type) give genuine, complementary axes for analyzing support burden and are largely well grounded in the ticket text. However nearly half the set consists of near-duplicate pairs (is_outage/is_outage_or_incident, system_component/system_component_affected, blocker_type/blocker_or_dependency, data_risk/data_risk_or_exposure, technical_root_cause/technical_root_cause_pattern) that restate each other with only shifted distributions, adding little leverage and even contradicting their twins on some rows. Grounding is generally sound for extractive/categorical columns; the root-cause columns show the most speculative, unsupported confident specifics.
